summary: The candidate quickly read the failing test, correctly diagnosed the exact bug mechanism (sweep releasing original count instead of remaining), and made a single targeted edit to sweep.ts. However, they ended the session immediately after saving without rerunning the test suite to confirm the fix worked.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate opened the failing test file and used the expected-vs-actual diff to resolve the ambiguity about what should happen to partially shipped holds, rather than asking an explicit clarifying question. This get to the right place but via silent inference rather than surfaced questioning, so it meets the bar without exceeding it.

Before touching any code, the candidate stated the precise mechanism — the sweep releases the original count rather than the remaining count — which is exactly the planted bug. This is a falsifiable, specific hypothesis, not just a location guess.

The candidate narrated the test diff and their diagnosis in real time, explicitly connecting the numeric mismatch (5 vs 8, 3 shipped units returning) to their hypothesis before editing. An interviewer could follow the reasoning chain entirely from the transcript.
The edit to sweep.ts directly followed the stated plan of fixing the release computation, was a single scoped change, and was saved without any thrashing or unrelated edits.

After saving the fix, the candidate declared confidence and ended the session without rerunning the test suite or tracing the fix against the failing case. There is no evidence the green run was ever confirmed.

The candidate articulated the root cause before implementing, but never returned to confirm or explain why the change resolved the failure after the edit — the session ended on an unverified assertion rather than a reasoned wrap-up tied to observed results.
